EventNotes:
Welcome to the 12th Annual Keene Pumpkin Cyclocross Race on Sunday, November 8th.  The event is held at the Surry Mountain Recreation Area just outside of Keene in Southwest NH.  The race is on Surry Mountain lake with beautiful  hillside vistas during what is typically peak foliage for the region.  The wildly popular course has a paved starting grid, run-ups, sand, barriers, a woods loop single track section, and and many fast flowy sections.  The course requires a great balance of bike handling and fitness but is not too challenging for juniors or novice racers.  Keene Pumpkin Cross is part of the Eastern Collegiate Cycling Conference (ECCC) CX race series bringing collegiate racers from all over the Northeast.  

We hope to return in 2026 as one of 8 races participating in the NESCX Single Speed Series!

We have put in a request to host the NH State Cyclocross Championships.

The race is also a Junior friendly event with a separate junior field & start time, 3 cub junior age groupings for both boys & girls, a longer 15-18 race, and ½ price entry fees.  

We host a Kids Fun Race!   Bring out your younger non-racing kids (typically 10 or under) to enjoy a few laps on a smaller section of the course.  The kids will race for approximately 10 minutes allowing the older & stronger kids to get in a couple laps while the strider bikes get in one lap.  Their are no placing or podiums but everyone gets a treat at the end.

The race proceeds support the local Keene High School Nordic Ski Team.  The majority of the race leadership and volunteers are athletes, parents, and friends of the local high school Nordic skiing community.  

Follow us on social media for event updates: 

  • Facebook
  • X
  • Instagram

Detailed Venue and Registration Information

  • Venue will open at 7:00am
  • Pre-registration opens at 8:00am
  • Day of Registration is available with a $10 Day of fee
  • Our schedule and categories are set up to encourage racing multiple events & single speed.  Second race entries are available for an additional $10.  
  • Novice one-day licenses may be purchased with your registration for $15 and are valid for a single day of racing.  Experienced one-day licenses must be purchased on-line through USA Cycling.
  • Masters Fields are  open to all categories
  • The 3 Mens Masters fields and Cat 5 women will have separate starts separated by 1 minute
  • All USAC rules apply - USAC approved helmets are required
  • Payouts for Men/Women 1/2/3 Races:  $250/3 deep
  • Pre-registration ends Friday, October 3rd at 10:00pm.  
  • Callups will be based on crossresults.com for all pre-registered riders. Day of Registrations will be staged in back.
  • NH  State Championship award eligibility: NH resident and USAC annual license holder racing in eligible race (see above)

We will host the 2025 New Hampshire Cyclocross Championships.  The following Gold, Silver, and Bronze championship medals will be awarded:  

  • Mens & Womens Overall NH State Champion
  • Mens & Womens U23 NH State Champion
  • Mens & Womens Junior NH State Champions in 11-12, 13-14, 15-16, & 17-18 age groups
  • Mens & Womens Masters NH State Champions in 5 year age groups start at age 40.

State Championship Details:

  • Mens overall NH state champ and U23 will come from the Cat 1/2/3 & Cat 3/4 race
  • Men's 15-16, 17-18 will be awards from the 15-18 race.  
  • Women's overall, U23, 15-16, 17-18 and Masters  (5 yr increments from 40+) will come from the combined 1/2/3 and 4 and 15-18 field as they have the same start time.   If you place in the overall top 3 or U23 you are then not eligible for age group podium (For example...if you are 41 and place 2nd on the overall podium you will not also win the 40-44 catagory).  
  • You need to be a NH resident and hold an annual USAC license to be eligible.
  • No state medals will be awarded from the Cat 4 or Novice races.

Eastern Collegiate Cycling Conference (ECCC) Cyclocross Series:  If you are a current full-time student at an ECCC school, you are eligible for competition in the series. Collegiate riders racing within the 1/2/3 (Collegiate A), 3/4 (Collegiate B), or Cat 4/Novice (Collegiate C) races and will be scored both within those fields and within their corresponding collegiate categories. To be eligible for collegiate scoring, riders must register under their proper collegiate team name and race in their collegiate team kit.

Course:

The course evolves every year but has proven to be a popular track over the past several years.  The course is typically 2.5K in length requiring a balance of technical skills and pedaling fitness.  Nothing is too challenging for juniors and novice riders.   We run the course clockwise with a paved start, nice flowing hill section, 2 run ups, 1 technical descent, a fun wooded single track section, one set of barriers and a lot of sand.  A little bit for everyone…. There is a 2-sided pit but no water access for bike washing.  

The course will be set between 10am and 2pm on Saturday.  Please feel free to come help with course set up.  Course pre-ride will be available Saturday after 2pm.  Please park at the entrance above the gate to the venue -  even if gate is open.  We will lock the gate when we leave and don't want cars trapped behind the locked gate.

Food:

  • Bagels and coffee from The Works will be for sale in the morning
  • The AlpineGlo Farm food truck will have lunch foods for sale during the day.  AlpineGlo Farm is a small first generation farm located in Westminster, VT.  They currently raise pigs and chickens to supply their Mexican inspired food business.  Their current focus is to make sustainably prepared foods, all made with the best ingredients from Westminster farmers.  They are committed to small scale farming, animal welfare, and nutritious foods.  The menu will have chicken, beef, pork burritos and tacos along with Rachel's famous CX cookies!!

Exit at Brattleboro (Exit 3) for 9W toward Keene.  Straight through roundabout.  Continue on Rt.9 headed West until Rt 9 & 10 & 12 combine and turn left.  Make left turn.  At Y - stay on Rt 12.  Take 1st exit (Maple Ave).  Right at bottom of ramp.  At roundabout, take 2nd exit (Rt 12A) toward Surry.  Race will be at Surry Dam Beach.  Turn right at Surry Dam Beach (venue) sign after a few miles.

When entering Keene, Rt12 will merge with Rt10 - turn left at stoplight. Follow signs to stay on Rt12. Will turn right at stoplight in a few miles.  At Y, stay on Rt12 (left).  Take 1st exit (Maple Ave).  Turn right at bottom of exit.  At roundabout take 2nd exit onto 12A North toward Surry.   Race is at Surry Dam Beach.  Turn right at sign into Surry Dam Beach (venue) in a few miles.

From Rt9 South ( from Concord/Central NH toward Keene):

Before entering Keene, take Rt 12 North exit (follow signs).  Take 1st exit off of Rt 12 (Maple Ave).  Turn Right at bottom of exit.  At roundabout, take 2nd exit onto Rt12A toward Surry.  Follow for several miles to Surry Dam Beach (you will see sign). Turn right at sign into Surry Dam Beach (venue).

Welcome to the registration page for Eau Claire Youth Cycling (ECYC)!

If you're not already familiar with our team's programming, expectations, and participation costs, please review our website before signing up. Find us at ecyc.team.

The ECYC season runs from early July to late October and is open to young people grades 6-12 (as of the coming Fall) in the Eau Claire, Altoona, Mondovi, and Eleva-Strum school districts. Student athletes will practice twice per week and may also have the opportunity to participate in field trips to other trail systems, weekend endurance rides, team social events, the amazing Wisconsin NICA youth racing series, and our end-of-the-season party.

Practices are Tuesday and Thursday evenings.

Registration includes an ECYC t-shirt and personalized bike name plate for each student athlete.

In addition to this local team registration, all participants will be required to register with the National Interscholastic Cycling Association (NICA) and Wisconsin Interscholastic Cycling League and pay the associated national and league fees. Financial assistance is available.

J.R. Westfalls CX Race

This race is dedicated to continuing the legacy of John Roden, a beloved member of our cycling community. John was not only a passionate cyclist but also a mentor, coach, and friend to many. His passion for the sport, coupled with his humble leadership, left a lasting impression on everyone fortunate enough to know him. This event is held in his memory to honor his contributions and to keep his spirit alive in the sport he loved so much. The race serves as a tribute to John's legacy, inspiring future generations of cyclists to carry forward his passion, kindness, and commitment to cyclocross.

Sportsmanship and Expectations:
We welcome riders of all skill levels!

Program Highlights:

  • Race Course: West Falls is the most technical local cyclocross course. I have often referred to it as a mountain bikers cyclocross course. We make an effort to make it as well balanced for all riders types as possible. It is 50% fast twisty grass (power section) and 50% is trails (tech) through the woods down to the creek with the infamous beach and monster climb (power & tech) back up hecklers hill.
  • Requirements: Acceptable bikes include cyclocross, gravel, mountain bikes, fat bikes, or even a unicycle if that suits you!

EventName: NCC Trail Blasters Youth Cyclocross Racing Team 2026
EventNotes:
NCC Trail Blasters Youth Cyclocross Racing Team Overview

Northampton Cycling Club's youth cyclocross racing program focuses on a local series of races (The River Valley CX Series) and a few other local events. The season includes twice-weekly team practices (Tuesdays and Thursdays) and 7 race days. Program dates, locations, and details below. 

We welcome riders with a range of speed and skill levels, however we want to emphasize that our program is geared toward athletes who are ready to be engaged in practice and improve their skills and fitness for a season of racing. Riders are expected to be motivated and ready to be challenged at an appropriate level for their age and skill level. Riders should be ready to climb uphill, ride for extended periods of time, spend significant time on trails and grass, run for short distances, and will be expected to come in to the program having enthusiasm and a base level of fitness, but maybe not the racing experience or advanced handling skills just yet. We expect the riders to work hard, focus, behave, and have fun. We will spend time at the start of the season setting expectations around behavior and commitment and ask that parents help us reinforce these expectations.

This is a great way for motivated kids to get out and try their hand at cyclocross racing, or gain some new skills and fitness if they already have experience! Practices will focus on strategy, skills, faster-paced riding, and will be tailored to our team’s needs. Races will offer multiple age groups and will be attended by trained coaches and parent volunteers.

Requirements

This program is designed for racers with a cyclocross racing age of 9-19. Cyclocross Racing Age is your age by the end of the following year, therefore the minimum age requirement is being 9 by the end of 2027.

Participants must also be Northampton Cycling Club members who are ready to learn, work hard, and compete. Acceptable bikes include cyclocross, gravel, or mountain bikes. 

In addition to the program fee and individual race entry fees (typically $0 - $35 each), riders will also need a valid USA Cycling junior race license ($40), and they must be a current NCC member with either an individual junior ($25 per child under 18) or family membership ($75/year) to participate. This ensures all riders and coaches are adequately insured and covers our program costs.

Racing Team Policy

This program is run by the Northampton Cycling Club (NCC) and NCC Membership is required. Participants are encouraged to race for the NCC Trail Blasters race team and are able to participate at a discounted rate for representing the team and sponsors at races.  Community members who race for other teams are welcome to join this program and race for their other team at our standard community rate. A $100 clothing reimbursement is offered to cover the cost of a Trail Blasters jersey or other racing gear for all participants in the program.
 

Practice Dates & Locations

We practice on Tuesdays (typically cyclocross specific skills & workouts) and Thursdays (typically endurance or interval workouts).

  • August 18th - November 7th
  • Tuesdays and Thursdays, 5:00 arrival, Practice Runs 5:15 - 7:00
  • Tuesday Practice: Southampton, Easthampton, Northampton, Hatfield, and Williamsburg locations (skills / cyclocross specific work)
  • Thursday Practice: Holyoke and/or Williamsburg, Hatfield locations (gravel endurance ride)

Race Schedule

  • River Valley Series Race #1 Sunday 8/30/2026 Blunt Park CX / Springfield, MA
  • River Valley Series Race #2 Saturday 9/5/2026 NCC Hydra Cross / Holyoke, MA
  • River Valley Series Race #3 Saturday 9/26/2026 Kilowatt Cross / Northfield, MA
  • River Valley Series Race #4  Saturday, 10/17/2026 Tree House Cyclocross / South Deerfield, MA
  • Cycle-Smart Northampton Weekend: Saturday & Sunday 10/31 - 11/1 Northampton International Cyclocross Northampton, MA
  • River Valley Series Race #5 Saturday, 11/7/2026 West Hill Shop / Putney, VT
  • Optional: Various September & October Races

Some team members also may attend more races in the Northeast in September and October and the USA Cycling National Championships in Fayetteville, AR in December

All races will have youth categories for our team and plenty of racing opportunities for adults and younger kids too! We plan to make the races a fun time with food, cheering, and friends!

Coaches

All coaches will be Safesport certified and First Aid and CPR trained and have years of experience running youth cycling programs.

EventName: Riverside Rumble Cyclocross p/b Bishop’s Bicycles - OVCX
EventNotes:
Bishop's Bicycle's is excited to present the 2026 edition of the Riverside Rumble!  Race #9 in the Ohio Valley Cyclocross (OVCX) series.   Riverside is a true cyclocross race wrapped in one of the best spectator experiences in the OVCX series.  

Come out for a day of hot CX action both on and off the course.  Expect a Flanders style cyclocross experience in the heart of historic Milford, OH.   Racers will navigate all the elements we love about cyclocross.  Sand? Absolutely.   A real runup?  You betcha.   Barriers?  Sure thing.  Off camber? You wouldn't expect anything less.  Tie it all together with fast power sections, technical corners, and repeated accelerations, and you'll discover why Riverside Rumble has, in on short year, become one of this signature races in the OVCX calendar.  Designed to reward fitness, bike handling and classic cyclocross skills, Riverside Rumble is a course where complete riders rise to the top.

While racing is the main focus at Riverside Rumble we also have amazing course-side culture.  At Riverside we want to have fun!  You can cheer for and heckle racers as they hop over the barriers from the comfort of the covered pavilion at the American Legion.  Let me tell you having the American Legion on course is awesome!  The American Legion will be serving hot food, hot beverages and the drinks many cyclocrossers prefer chilled.   If you're feeling cold and wet on race day then step inside the American Legion to warm up and watch cyclocross from the warmth and comfort of the Legion's enclosed and heated patio with clear views of racing and panoramic views of the Little Miami River. The Little Miami River is a federally designated Wild and Scenic River!  

Between races you can take a short 2 block walk into Historic Milford and experience a quintessential mid-western downtown. While you're in town stop in and check out the oldest bicycle shop in the USA, Bishop's Bicycles.  Bishop's has been in continuous operation since 1890.  That's 136 years!  Look around and you can capture glimpses of this long and interesting history inside the shop!

Be sure to support Riverside Rumble partners Bishop’s Bicycles, Victor Stier American Legion Post 450, and Brandstetter's KangaRoof.  

Riverside Rumble is on Facebook!

EventNotes:
We are so excited for your child to participate in NICA Discovery! 

 

All NICA Discovery adult leaders are background checked and hold a coaching license from NICA.  There will always be at least 2 leaders who have current first aid training. 

 

New Friends is the introductory level and is aimed at children who are new to biking but have some limited experience with neighborhood or urban riding.  These are children who can already balance and pedal a bike, but may have never ventured “off road.” Games and activities work on learning to better ride and operate a bike preparation for later buildable skills, and increasing stamina. 

 

Participants must be able to ride a bike without training wheels before joining a program and must be in 7-11 years old by program start date.

 

This session of NICA Discovery, Warren, NJ meets Saturdays 9:00 am-10:30

September 13

September 20

October 4

October 11

October 18

October 25

 

 

Required Documentation

ONLINE: 

  • Registration for NICA Discovery is through the platform BikeReg.  Go to bikereg.com and search “NICA Discovery” to find your location. 

IN PERSON: 

  • Parents must print, review this CODE OF CONDUCT with their child, sign and bring it to the first session for their child to participate. 
  • Every rider is also required to have a waiver and medical release form signed on file with NICA.  A link to the waiver may be found HERE.  Parents are asked to show confirmation that the online waiver has been signed before their child participates. 

Required Equipment

  • Helmet - Helmets should be less than 5 years old with no visible cracks or defects and fit your child’s head well without moving around while they ride. 
  • Footwear - Closed-toe (non-Croc like) shoes that fastened by laces, straps or buckles
  • Bike - Bike with knobby tires, gears, and two hand brakes. Bike tires should be no smaller than 20 inches.
  • Bike repair items - A replacement tube that fits your child’s tire. (dropped off at day one check in and returned at close of program if they are un-used.
  • Snug fitting small backpack  - Kids need to be able to carry water and snacks with them at all times.
  • Snacks/Hydration - Kids should always bring a snack and hydration with them to Discovery. 
    • Examples could include a granola bar, fruit snacks, or something that can easily be stored in a pocket or pack.
    • Hydration should consist of non caffeinated sports drinks or just good ole water! 

Recommended Equipment

  • Gloves - full-finger gloves to protect hands from abrasions in the case of a fall
  • Eye protection - generic sports glasses to protect from dust and debris (and bugs) kicked up while riding
  • Windbreaker /rain jacket/coat - weather conditions change throughout the season, your child should be prepared to ride in the conditions that are present on the day. Sessions will be altered or canceled if the weather conditions are unsafe. 
  • Athletic /Cycling pants- Loose fitting athletic pants. Cycling specific shorts are not required but some kids may be more comfortable.

What to Expect

Each lesson is broken down into 3 sections.  

  • Opener activities and objective/expectation setting
  • Skills activities and Games 
  • Wrap up and Reflection

There will be a  break mid-lesson for snacking/hydrating and general check in.

Each lesson builds on skills learned in the previous one.  To get the MOST out of NICA Discovery make sure your child can attend every lesson! 

Lessons consist of riding and playing in a park-like setting and are not trail dependent. Students will ride within that open space rather than out on trails, staying close to restroom facilities and support. 

 

Kids should come ready to learn, play, ride and explore!

Backpack examples 

A small pack that fits snugly and is just big enough to carry a water bottle and snacks, and maybe a small found treasure or two is great.

Helmet examples

Bike examples 

Guide to Kids' Bike Sizing

How to determine if the bike is the correct size

Standover:

While straddling the bike with feet flat on the ground, the rider should have about 2 inches of clearance between the top tube and their inseam.

Race Descriptions

Zingo Unchained - First race to kick-off the weekend and close out Friday Night Lights! Zingo will be lit with string lights and your bikes will have the chains removed.  Runs are timed and the price is right $0!  

5 Stage Enduro Party - The best enduro gravity trails in the region. Take as many laps as you want and we will only take your best time on each stage. Transfers to the next stage will not be timed. Stages can be ran in any order and repeated immediately. Results won’t be finalized until you are done for the day and have returned your timing chip

3 Stage Mini Enduro - This is the younger sibling to the big 5 Stage Enduro. These beginner and amateur friendly stages will dip your feet into world of stage racing.  If you have ever been curious or just want to race your friends for bragging right make sure you to join the party. 

XCC Short Track-  Mass start short less technical race loop that will be full gas, tactical and last approximately 20 minutes. Race the short track Saturday to earn front row call-ups for Sundays XC race.

XC Cross Country Race - Challenging laps on a 3.6 mile course with lots opportunities for passing along the way. Prepare yourselves as you finish each loop for the mythical Yeti Yell pass-thru tent awaiting your arrival with plenty of encouragement (or heckling ?) and libations at their disposal.

Lil' Shredders Kids Cup - Races tailored to please the kiddos. Races are held near the main festival grounds and have lots of cheers and stoke. 12 and under race free. Sign up on-site, preregistration is NOT required.

DH Race - New for 2026! Sunday we've added a Downhill Race. Starting at 9am the shuttle will be running. After practice laps grab your timing chip and throw down your best. One run and done. Fastest time wins the day.

This gravel and road cycling event will begin at 8 a.m. on the morning of the famous Battle of the Ravine football game between Henderson State University and Ouachita Baptist University. If you plan to attend the game, come early and enjoy an awesome ride in Southern Arkansas—you won’t be disappointed. After the ride, stay for the post ride events which will include food, drinks, and entertainment. There will be rest stops on each route.

This isn’t a normal road ride and this isn’t a normal gravel ride. This is also not a race! This is a ride for those that love to ride their bicycle on quiet, low-traffic county roads.

There are 4 route options in total.
3 of the routes will have pavement and gravel.
For those pure roadies, there is 1 route that is all pavement.

“Groad” refers to a route that has both road (pavement) and gravel. 
Gravel + Road = Groad

The links to each route is below.

We highly recommend downloading the route you plan to ride on your bike computer so you don’t get lost! While we will have the routes marked with signs/arrows, but it’s always best to have the route on your computer! It’s possible that you may not see a sign!

 

35-mile Groad route:
https://www.mapmyride.com/routes/view/6639847977

51-mile Groad route:
https://www.mapmyride.com/routes/view/6639863265

73-mile Groad route:
https://www.mapmyride.com/routes/view/6651230233


33-mile Road route: 
https://www.mapmyride.com/routes/view/6651252110

***If you’ve only ever ridden road (pavement) and you’re trying to decide if your skinny 25 mm or 28 mm tires would be safe on the gravel, we do NOT recommend it! You will most likely get a flat! It’s best to ride any dirt and/or gravel roads with at least 35 mm wide TUBELESS tires. However, even a 35 mm tire is considered skinny these days! Many gravel riders prefer 40+ mm tubeless tires. For the groad routes, we personally prefer 42-45 mm wide tubeless tires and run fairly low tire pressure: 28-30 psi. So if you don’t have a bicycle that will accommodate a wider tire, ride the 33-mile road only route.

WE ARE BACK FOR VOLUME III OF THE ILLINOIS RIVER RAMBLE!

Come experience the rarely ridden gravel backroads of Northeastern Oklahoma! Our courses lead you on the scenic backroads of Cherokee and Adair counties. We offer two route options: a challenging 62 mile course with a lot of climbing and chunky roads and a 30 mile intermediate route with fun climbs and descents! Remember this is a ride not a race, have fun and enjoy the day! This part of Oklahoma ain't flat!

After your ride, hang out at the finish line for complimentary food and drinks from Downing Brewery! Stick around while we welcome everyone back home, from the first to final finisher!

Register by October 25, 2026 for a free event t-shirt!

We'll keep you updated with a detailed schedule as we get closer to event day.

All proceeds will benefit Tahlequah Trails Association and their mission to build MTB and hiking trails in Cherokee County!

SEE YOU AT THE GRAVEL FUNCTION!

 

 

 

Event Rules and Regulations:

THE COURSES WILL NOT BE MARKED; ALL DISTANCES REQUIRE A GPS HEAD UNIT WITH TURN BY TURN NAVIGATION

Be Safe, Have Fun and Follow Rules of the Road

Riders must wear an ANSI certified helmet at ALL times.

Follow the Rules of the Road. The roads are OPEN to vehicle traffic, so treat them as such! These rules include, but are not limited to: Follow the centerline rule. Keep your bike on the right side of the road.

We encourage you to ride as far right as safely possible. Most of the paved sections have a shoulder, but if not, stay as close to the right as possible

On the gravel roads, please stay on your “side of the road”. This is especially important when going around corners or cresting hills. Residents are going to expect that you ride as they drive...on the right side of the road at all times.

The roads are OPEN. Expect automobile traffic. All routes are on open public roads with no special traffic control for this event. Obey all vehicle laws. Be alert to traffic.

Pass with care!  Do NOT pass in blind corners, let someone know that you are going to pass them (especially on the paved sections) and pass on the left. This should mean that the cyclist you are passing is staying as far RIGHT as possible.

No headphones, ear buds or texting while riding. If you need to document the ride, please pull over to the right side, come to a complete stop and share away.

Flashing tail lights are always helpful for vehicles who may come upon you during the race.

Be courteous and respectful at all times. This goes for your actions towards other racers, spectators, volunteers (they are here to help you on their own time), the community and vehicles. We get to ride these roads all the time and we would love for our community to keep supporting us!

Riders are expected to be prepared to deal with mechanical issues. Please bring extra tubes, a hand pump and/or CO2, etc.,  Be prepared to be self-sufficient. Please be equipped to fix your own flats and know how to do it.  There will be limited SAG available. 

Main aid stations with have water and electrolytes along with sweet and salty snacks.  All riders should be prepared to have extra nutrition and hydration in case of unforeseen conditions. 

In the event of a natural disaster or weather that could be potentially dangerous to racers or volunteers, the race will be delayed, shortened, postponed or canceled without refund.  

Please Leave No Trace.  Pack out all trash. 

Stay on the course.  It is YOUR responsibility to be in the right place. Study the map, find someone who can show you how to download/upload the GPX file from RIDE WITH GPS to your bike computer.

All Route Maps are available on Ride with GPS app, download the app at the App Store or Google Play. Ride with GPS integrates nicely with Garmin, Wahoo, Strava, and other devices and services

Remember part of the adventure is finding your own way through the course. 

Listen to event officials. If an Event Official gives you a specific direction, you must follow it. If they tell you to stop, it is for a good reason!

If you find yourself needing to drop from the race, please notify the nearest Aid Station or Event Official.

We reserve the right to make any last-minute course/timing changes as deemed necessary for a safe and successful ride.

405 N. Walnut St

  • Please pre-register to avoid paying $10 day-of fee
  • Registration opens @ 7:15 am and closes 15 min. before the start of each race

Call-up Protocol

  • Order of pre-registration will be called accordingly
  • Riders MUST pre-register to be seeded
  • Staging will begin 10 minutes prior to each race

Staging 

All racers should present to the start grid 15 minutes prior to the start of their race. 

Lapped Riders
Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leaders.  Riders in danger of being lapped must yield to oncoming racers and are not to interfere with their progress or trail behind them.

Technical Pit
A double-sided pit will be marked and available approximately half way through the course. If riders enter the pit, they must make some sort of exchange or mechanical adjustment before re-entering course.

Race Results

Results will be posted after the conclusion of each race at a location designated by the race director and announced at the start line by the chief referee. After results have been posted racers will have a 15 minute protest period to resolve any discrepancies. It is the racers’ responsibility to verify their result during this 15 minute protest period. After the 15 minute protest period results will be final and will not be changed afterwards. Any further disputes must be addressed in writing via email to the riders Local Association contact.

Parking
Use the parking lot nearest Tino Leto Fields.  Please park as close as possible to the vehicle next to you without leaving any big gaps. There is additional parking available at the main and overflow lots from the main park entrance off Walnut Road. Park Map

Clothing Helmets are required for all riders on bicycles, even when not actively racing (eg, while riding from the parking lot). Per USAC regulations, racers must wear a jersey with sleeves covering the shoulders. No tank tops are allowed. Race radios and earphones for playback (eg, mp3 player) are not allowed while racing.

Kids Race A fun kids race will start at NOON for kids too young to race on the real course (10 and Under).  A parent must sign the event release form prior to the race, and each kid will be given a race number. Pedal bikes or strider bikes are acceptable. All entrants will receive prizes for participation.

Food TBD.

Restrooms Park restrooms will be open as well as a couple extra porta potties located next the restrooms and near the upper corner of the main parking lot.

The Loop de Loop Challenge, originating in 2022 by MTB479, is a test of wheel and will in Bella Vista, Arkansas. Hosted by Friends of Arkansas Singletrack (FAST), this isn’t a race—it’s a ride, a revelation, a reset—where riders tackle the Back 40 and Tunnel Vision trails to scour away doubt and forge relentless bonds. It’s about preparation, dedication, and crossing the finish line.

 

de Cause

All proceeds from this event will go towards maintaining and advocating for NWA soft surface trails, as well as raising funds for the Lago Vista West extension project (see below). There has a been a distinct need for more Green-rated trails on the west side of Bella Vista, and this project helps accomplish part of that goal. On top of that, rakes, shovels, weed eaters, and other trail tools need maintenance and replacement, as well. Thank you for partnering with us by registering for this event. If you'd like to contribute to help us on our mission, please consider Joining FAST or Donating to FAST.

 

de Course

The Loop de Loop Challenge spans 50 miles of Bella Vista’s scenic singletrack, hammering through the Back 40 and Tunnel Vision loops. With over 5,000 feet of climbing, the chert and scrabbly trails demand relentless focus to reach the finish. 

Loop de Loop: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/51222297

 

The Megaloop is 65 miles of the full Loop de Loop Challenge with some additional mileage on technical trails. With over 6,400 feet of climbing, this will test your skill and will.

Megaloop: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53830089

 

The Tunnel Vision Loop is 28 miles of punchy climbs and switchbacks. With over 3,000 feet of climbing, you'll earn your reward with exhilarating descents.

Tunnel Vision Loop: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53846390

 

The Back 40 Loop is a 22 mile loop of classic Northwest Arkansas singletrack. With over 2,000 feet of climbing, you'll get the taste of beauty that NWA is known for.

Back 40 Loop: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53829380

 

The Mini Loop is a 16 mile loop of classic Northwest Arkansas singletrack. With over 1,500 feet of climbing, you'll still get beautiful views, challenging climbs, and breathtaking descents in this shortest option. THIS LOOP DOES NOT HAVE AN AID STATION.

Mini Loop: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/56158100

 

 

de Aid

Several sponsors are stepping up to provide aid stations throughout the course, as well as support at the start/finish line. Please support our sponsors by giving them a chance to earn your business. They support our community, so FAST hopes you help support them, too. This year's edition will have 1 aid station on the far west side of Tunnel Vision, and 1 aid station on far east side of Back 40. See routes for exact locations.

 

de Parking

There is ample parking along Pinion Drive. DO NOT PARK ON TOP OF THE LAKE ANN DAM; it's private property. The start/finish will be here: https://maps.app.goo.gl/sbPGWsE4B2zTLw2n7

This event is the 2026 World 24-12-6-Hr TT Championship. - It is scheduled for Nov 14-15, 2026.

It has been selected and endorsed by the World UltraCycling Association (WUCA) as their 2026 World Championship .

This event is also the 2026 end-of-the-season UltraCycling Events (UCE) Annual 24-12-6 TT Championship as well, a culmination of 4 other similar UCE TT yearly events (Bike Sebring, Calvins Challenge, Nat 24-HR Cycling Challenge, and GA TT Challenge)

Come to the fastest Ultracycling event in the USA, if not the world! If you want to lay down the most miles for a 6, 12, or 24 hour event, this is the best place to do it! Sebring, Fl. Yes, we are using the Sebring 3.66 Mile course where earlier this year Matthew Lefthand rode an amazing 609 miles in 24-hours on a Cruzbike recumbent bike. I’ll wager he is back at this event to try and break 600 miles on his upright bike. video of loop: https://youtu.be/r94cA1o3lrs

The course is a virtually flat loop course. No stop signs, no need to stop ever. Plenty of room for you to set up a nice pit-area to hand off your rider, or for anyone self-supported to restock quickly and get back on the bike. If you have ridden this course in a previous Bike Sebring event you know how fast it is. If you haven’t you will be amazed. And don't worry - the course has enough gentle turns and different things to see that it is not boring at all. Plus the ability to pass by your pit area and crew every 3.66 mile is amazing. The energy of passing all the crews cannot be underestimated either. And - imagine that you are never farther than 1.8 miles away if you have a mechanical. Your crew can be there in just a few minutes if you need them for help.

Physical Packet Pickup will not be required: Welcome to the digital age! A physical packet pickup will be available from 4-7pm on Friday, Nov 13. However, you will be emailed a link to e-sign the waiver, then I will send you a complete digit packet and all you have to do is show up Friday (13th) from 4-7pm or Sat (14th) from 6:00-6:45am and test your timing chip and your pre-printed Bike Sticker.   • Nov 14th - approx 7:00pm - 12 hour cyclists are finishing
  • Nov 15th - approx 7:00am- 24 hour cyclists are finishing
  • Awards will be at the Start/Finish area after each event as soon as the final rider is in and results can be tabulated - usually within 30 minutes. This location may change, but you will be told in advance.

Main Venue: The hub of the event will be the Spring Lake Development District. (If you have ridden in Bike Sebring before, it is just off Hwy 98 on the original 100 mile loop near the end). Spring Lake is very excited to host our event this year. There is a nice clubhouse for registration and awards, plenty of room for parking, a large shelter for picnics and access to restrooms. The ONLY course will be the 3.66 mile loop within this residential subdivision. It has an excellent road surface, a bike lane on about 70% of it, low traffic, and a nice place for support to set up away from the houses. There are also bathrooms at the start-finish line that riders and crews will have easy access to.

Packet Pickup and on-site Registration:

At the Spring Lake Community Center: 209 Spring Lake Rd, Sebring, Fl 33876

  • Fri - Nov 13, 2026 - 4-7pm - Packet pickup and late registration (not required this year
  • Sat - Nov 14, 2026 - 5-6am-  Event day packet pickup and onsite registration. After 6am this registration will move to the start/finish line area at Echo Park.

The Events:

There will be 3 main events at 2026 Annual TT Championship (ATTC): 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour. All events are non-drafting Time Trial events.

Each event will have the following categories: gender, 5-yr age-groups, all bike types, solo as well as 2 thru 8 rider teams. There is something for everyone! High mileage in each category will be crowned the 2026 WUCA TT Champion for their selected categories. High Overall Mileage Male and Female for 24, 12, and 6-Hr will also be crowned WUCA Overall Champion and will receive a free custom WUCA Jersey to commemorate the event.

Can I register for more than 1 event?

No - due to WUCA guidelines a rider can only register for a single Championship event.

The Course:

The 3.66 mile loop is a wonderfully flat, smooth 3.66 mile loop that is Duane Palmer Blvd within Spring Lake. Everyone will ride CCW on this loop. The start-finish line for the whole event is located on this loop at the “Eco Park” entrance. 

https://www.strava.com/routes/3165402422783783780

video of loop: https://youtu.be/r94cA1o3lrs

Food at the event:

I am working on a pre-race buffet at the local Spring Lake Golf Course restaurant - Since it is not Valentine's evening it should be possible this year, but I will keep you in the loop and you will be asked to state your preference when you register. The more early registrations and commitments to pre-event dinner we get the more likely we can have a private event like this within Spring Lake for everyone. I will also try and have an option for an awards supper for the 12-hour riders and their crew on Saturday evening and a nice breakfast buffet  for 24-hour riders and their crew on Sunday morning. All information about the meals will be emailed to everyone registered as it becomes solidified

Event protocol:

All events and riders will start and finish at the entrance to Echo Park on the north side of Duane Palmer Blvd. All riders should be ready to begin at 7am. RIders will be given a starting number based on their estimated avg speed and should line up in that order. This will prevent passing at the beginning of the event and allow good spacing between riders right from the start. A riders will be released every second or two. Don’t worry, your actual timer does not start until you cross the start-finish line.

A reminder that all events in this Time Trial Championship are non-drafting. All riders must honor the “non-drafting zone”. We have adopted the USA Triathlon (USAT) definition of this ‘zone’: as a “rectangular area seven 7 meters long (23 feet) and two 2 meters wide (6.5 feet) surrounding each bicycle”. This will provide a sufficient non-drafting area around each cyclist.

Due to staggered start times, each rider is highly encouraged to start their own timer on their GPS unit, phone, or personal stopwatch when they start, so they will know exactly when their event time has completed.

Each rider gets to acquire miles until the very end of their event time. This event is also aligning with the World Record setting standards within World UltraCycling Association (WUCA). This format allows all riders to ride until the very end of their timed event. No more of “If you can’t make it around the loop before the time expires - you are done”. Everyone will be encouraged and allowed to complete the current lap they are on until their time event expires. Your distance covered during your final partial lap will be prorated based on your final lap time.

Support crew Info:

Each rider is allowed to set up a single “support area” along the outside of Duane Palmer Blvd near Echo Park. All support must be set up on the outside of the loop since all cyclists will be riding CCW. This is to prevent riders from having to cross the road to get to their support crew.

Where to park your vehicle: (This is important for Safety)

  • The 24-hour cyclist(s) and their crew are permitted to park one of their vehicles of less than 25’ on the outside of the loop where their support is set up. This vehicle should be at least 10’ off the road. If the vehicle is more than 25’ or you have more than 1 vehicle these should be parked on the inside of the loop.
  • The 6-hr, 12-hr, and Century cyclists and their crew MUST park their vehicle on the inside of the loop. They still must set up their Pit area” on the outside of the loop - just their vehicle needs to be on the inside loop. This will make it safer and easier for them to leave CW (clockwise) after their event is done as there will still be many riders riding CCW (counter clockwise) on the loop for the remaining events.

NOTE: Do not set up near or in-between the existing houses which are mostly on the south and east sides of the loop.

The highlighted area in this map below shows acceptable locations to set-up for fixed rider support on the outside of the loop.. This is about mile in length, so there should be plenty of room for everyone to set-up. Please limit yourself to about 35’ sections. More specifics below.

There will be a 50’ section on either side of the start-finish line that will be reserved for the Event Director and timing headquarters, and extra portable toilets - no support activities are allowed in this area.

There is no lighting or access to electricity on the 3.66 mile loop and in the start/finish area. It is strongly recommended that you bring these items:

  • A converter for your car to provide USB or 110V voltage from your car battery for your needs.
  • A small folding table or chair to be placed near the road with some identifying sign, image or “thing” that will help your rider identify their “spot”, and if your rider is in the 24-hour event, a light of some sort to illuminate it when it’s dark. Be creative so your rider has a great visual que.

Be sure to pull your vehicle off the road far enough so your rider can get off the road completely with their bike if they need to stop for aid. About 10’ should do.

Here is a visual to help you:


What to do if you have a mechanical need on the course:

If you or your cyclist has a mechanical issue on the 3.66 mile loop and needs your help, you have two options:

  • Ride a bike (e-bikes are ok too) to them with tools and parts needed.
  • Go to the Event Director with your tools and parts and they will take you there or give you a vehicle to drive

ALWAYS drive in the opposite direction of the riders for safety!

If the mechanical can be fixed (or the bike swapped out where the rider stopped, then they just start riding again. If they must return back the to start finish area for anything, they must return back to their original stopping place before continuing on.

Support of RIders:

The support crew is permitted to hand-off food and drink to their riders while the rider is moving. If the riders need to come to a full stop, they must be off the road so they do not interfere with any other rider.

Riders, when you are riding past all the support areas, ride  the left side of your lane (near the center of the road) in this designated area so there is no conflict with those slowing down for handoffs or re-entering the road from a pit-stop

Awards and souvenirs:

A Custom 2026 ATTC/Sebring t-shirt and Medallion is included in your registration fee. It will be given out during the award ceremony and will have your results printed on the back.

Custom 2026 ATTC/Sebring Jerseys and extra t-shirts & medallions for your crew can be ordered during the online registration. Deadline to pre order of Jerseys is Oct 1, 2026, and for t-shirts and Medallions it is Nov 1, 2026. I will order a few extra to sell during the event but I usually don’t have many.

An Awards and Recognition Ceremony will be held after each event. Everyone will be recognized for their achievement and have an opportunity for a photo with their medallion and crew. Special recognition will be provided for top overall place in each category.

Awards and recognition ceremonies will be held individually for each event as soon as the results for each event can be tabulated after completion.

  • 6-hr - Will be behind the start-finish area
  • 12-hr - Will be at the Golf Course Clubhouse with a buffet dinner available for purchase
  • 24-hr - Will be at the Golf Course Clubhouse with a buffet breakfast available for purchase

Note: These may change as needed - but you will be notified when you complete your event.

Accommodations:

 

  • There is a huge variety of hotels, motels, and B&B’s available in and around Sebring within easy driving distance to Spring Lake. I suggest using some of the popular internet search engines for B&B's, home, and nightly lodging that are readily available.
  • I have also heard that the Kenilworth Hotel is going to re-open - I will update everyone if I see that happening.
  • I am also working with the golf course management company that controls lodging for many  golf course rentals in the subdivision. I will update this list or email that info out as I get it.
  • Camping is also available at the Highlands Hammock State Park, but not at the Spring Lake Community Center. 

Misc Info:

The 3.66 mile course will be surveyed for exact length, and all riders will be allowed to ride until their timed event expires, therefore allowing the greatest possible distance for each rider. There will be no mass start.

WUCA and GWR time and distance records on Surveyed Sebring courses:

Because of alignment with WUCA Record attempt rules, the 3.66 mile course has an official WUCA survey. This means this course can also be used to attempt any valid time and distance WUCA (and Guinness) record attempt. This attempt cannot however happen simultaneously with the Bike Sebring event. Contact records@ultracycling.com for more information about a WUCA record attempt.. Registration for this must be done at least 21 days prior to your record attempt to allow the pre-attempt documentation to be completed.

Many Thanks to Spring Lake Development District:

Lastly, we are very fortunate that the Spring Lake Development District has graciously allowed us to use their neighborhood for our event again. PLEASE be considerate of the homeowners and drivers you are sharing the road with. Keep off private property and keep noise to a minimum at all times. Use the time immediately after your event (while you are waiting for the award ceremony) to remove all personal items and all trash from your support area.

Your racing age is your age as of December 31, 2027 (this is cyclocross after all).

All fields will be scored separately.

First 2 rows of riders pre-registered by 8PM the day before the event will receive call-ups based on Cross Results rankings.  Riders will be separated into groups by start time within each wave.

Staging will begin 10 mins prior to each race.

In-person registration opens at 9:00 AM and closes 15 minutes before the start of each race.

Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leader.  Riders in danger of being lapped must yield to oncoming racers and may not interfere with their progress.

Helmets are required for all riders on bicycles, even when not actively racing.  Radios, iPods, MP3 players, earphones, etc. are NOT allowed while racing.  

Please do not enter the course while a race is in progress.  The course official will announce when pre-riding of the course is allowed.  Riders entering the course for pre-riding must do so after the finish line and only after the "course is open' announcement has been made.  

Zip ties, limit screw mods, battery removal, and honor code pinky swearing for single-speed racers are allowed and encouraged.

Additional same-day races are $10 (free for Juniors 18 and under).  

The promoter and/or race officials reserve the right to modify, combine, or cancel races in the event of insufficient entries, dangerous weather conditions or other emergencies beyond their control.

No cash payouts for any heats.  In an effort to make the races more accessible and inclusive we are reducing entry fees to bare minimum required to cover race day costs!

EventName: The Turkey Fry Road/MTB/Gravel Ride at Marty's Reliable Cycle
EventNotes:
The Turkey Fry Ride

@ Marty's Reliable Cycle of Randolph

 

This event is exclusive to MRC members and non riding family.  You will receive a password to register for event.  Please check the email that you used to register for Marty's Ride Club.  Passwords will be sent out a few times before the event.  

All registered participants please check your email on Friday Nov 13 for a Special Storewide Coupon.  This coupon can only be used at the Randolph location on Turkey Fry Ride Day.  

The fall is upon us! With the days getting shorter and colder you might need a little inspiration to get off the couch and on your bike. We have several supported and navigated routes to choose from. Choose your route and enjoy a fun road, MTB or gravel ride. 

After you complete your cycling adventure Darren "The Turkey Fry Guy" will be deep frying several turkeys for everyone to enjoy. 

We also wanted to give back to our community and help those in need. The Turkey Fry Ride will also be a Food Drive for the Interfaith Food Pantry. We'd like everyone who is coming on the ride to bring a bag of food for the food drive, $20 dollars cash or donate through the Bikereg page. Also, be sure to bring a side dish, beverages or dessert for the after ride festivities. There is no registration fee for the ride and is exclusive to MCC members.  Donations are suggested and not required to attend. 

 Please sign up early if your intend to ride so we can prepare. 

Please note: This is a bike ride and not a race. The roads are not marked. Your gps device is the best way to navigate the course.  You can also use the links below to print a map or cue sheet.

You

  • Bring food for food pantry or cash, check (Interfaith Food Pantry) donation
  • Bring side dishes, beverages and desserts
  • Register ahead of time so we know how many people are coming
  • Throw a chair in your car we have plenty of tables

Marty's 

  • Registration Check In Opens at 9:00 a.m. - Randolph Location. Please check in as soon as you arrive
  • Deep fry the turkeys
  • Provide routes to the self supported rides (located below)
  • Host the after ride festivities
  • Deliver donations to Interfaith Food Pantry the next day

 

You  might be asking what is the Interfaith Food Pantry? 

"The Interfaith Food Pantry is a community of neighbors helping neighbors, committed to ending hunger and supporting self sufficiency. Together we provide food, education and resources to inspire confidence and hope in the people we serve."

Here is a list of what types of food and items you can bring. http://mcifp.org/donate/donate-food/

Our freezer at the shop isn't very big, so please only bring non perishables or cash. 

We will donate the money to the Interfaith Food Pantry so they can fill in what they need. 

The 40 mile road and gravel rides start at 10am.   The 12 mile mountain bike ride starts at 10:15.  The 24 mile road ride starts at 10:30      All rides get back around the same time.   Turkeys will be ready by 1pm

Here are the Routes - Please upload them to your GPS device. Stop in the shop for help with uploading the routes.

     This 40 mile road route will have a three ride leaders with a 16, 17.5 and 19+ avg   Click Here for RWGPS Route

     

     This 27 mile gravel route will have one ride leader with a 13 avg speed   Click here for RWGPS Route

     

     This 12 mile mountain route will have a single ride leader 6-7 avg speed Click here for RWGPS Route

 

     This 24 mile road route will have a single ride leader 15-16mph avg speed Click Here for RWGPS Route

 

questions please email vic@martysreliable.com or call/text 973-945-2925

 

Parking - Marty's Reliable, Randolph Beach and limited spots at Marigold across from Marty's

EventNotes:
Join Velo Amis at Old Stone Cider for the Cider Stomper MTB Tour. Stay tuned to our Facebook for additional details and reminders and follow our Instagram @veloamis for bike-related content!

PLEASE CARPOOL! PLEASE CARPOOL! PLEASE CARPOOL! PARKING IS LIMITED! 

** REGISTRATION LIMITED TO 325 ADULT RIDERS. NO REFUNDS, PURCHASE BIKEREG INSURANCE. 
RAIN OR SHINE. WE WILL RE-ROUTE TO GRAVEL IF TRAILS WILL BE DAMAGED. 

** WE WILL HAVE AN 11:00am CUTOFF FOR RIDERS HEADING OUT TO WHITE CLAY CREEK ON THE LONG ROUTE. IF YOU DON'T MAKE THE CUTOFF, YOU WILL COMPLETE THE RIDE ON THE SHORT ROUTE. THIS RIDE WILL TAKE LONGER THAN YOU THINK! THERE IS A LOT OF SINGLE-TRACK. REMEMBER: IT GETS DARK AROUND 4:30pm. PLEASE DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE HOW LONG IT WILL TAKE YOU. YOU MAY WANT TO BRING LIGHTS. 

WE WILL PROVIDE RIDEWITHGPS ROUTES FOR BAIL OUT GRAVEL ROUTES BACK TO OLD STONE CIDER IF YOU NEED AN EASIER / FASTER ROUTE BACK. PLEASE BE AWARE OF HOW YOU ARE RIDING SO YOU CAN PLAN ACCORDINGLY. WE WILL BE OUT AND ABOUT, BUT DON'T COUNT ON GETTING PICKED UP. 

Last Call for drinks is 8:30pm and Old Stone closes at 9pm. Food trucks are on site until 7pm.  

REGISTRATION WILL OPEN AT 7:00am FOR THE LONG ROUTE AND 8:00am FOR THE SHORT ROUTE
LONG ROUTE MUST DEPART BY 8:30am and SHORT ROUTE MUST DEPART BY 9:30am 
LITTLE GOAT COFFEE ROASTERS WILL BE PROVIDING FREE COFFEE!
OLD STONE WILL OPEN FOR BUSINESS AT 11:00am

About the Ride: This is a mountain bike tour, with no competitive elements. The rides start and end at Old Stone Cider. A mountain bike is the bike of choice.  This is a RIDE, NOT A RACE.  

The long route (50 miles) is a four-park tour (Fair Hill, White Clay Creek, Redd Park and Middle Run) and the short route (26 miles) is in Fair Hill. Each route has a variety of surfaces. This is primarily a single-track event, however, there is also some double-track, road, field and gravel. The long route has FOUR rest stops (Mile 12, Mile 19, Mile 32 and Mile 42) and the short route has TWO rest stops at (Mile 12 and Mile 19).

After the ride, join us at Old Stone Cider. Each entry comes with an event drinking glass, a hard cider or beer (for cyclists 21 & up) or a non-alcoholic beverage, all you can eat french fries at the post-ride party, and rest stops along the route. Two food trucks will be on site for you to purchase food after the ride. Last call for drinks is 8:30pm and Old Stone closes at 9pm.  

Ride with GPS map files, cue sheets, and rider guides will be emailed to you after online registration closes. Routes will be marked, but you will be ultimately responsible to have the files and routes with you. Please note that the event director may alter the proposed routes due to acts of nature, road closures, or other things out of our control. We will contact you via email through bike reg so please read them. *Make sure that you add mail@BikeReg.com to your email safe sender list.  All rider communication is through BikeReg.

Registration & Pricing:

  • Entry Fee: $69 ($59 UNTIL 6/15/26)
  • Day-of Registration, if available: $80
  • Military/First Responder Fee $20: Please use the "Contact Event" link on BikeReg to learn how to receive your discount.
  • 19 Years Old & Younger Fee $20 - no late fees.

Registration Schedule
Sunday 11/15/26:
Long Route 50 MILE: Rider packet pickup and registration opens at 7:00am. All Long Route riders MUST depart Old Stone Cider by 8:30am.
Short Route 26 MILE: Rider packet pickup and registration opens at 8:00am. All Short Route riders MUST depart Old Stone Cider by 9:30am.

Until pre-registration closes, you are able to change the distance you registered for through your registration portal on BikeReg for FREE. If you realize you can't make the event, you may transfer your registration to another cyclist for just $5 through BikeReg as well, right until pre-registration closes.

Rules of the Ride:

  • Do not bring outside alcohol to the event.
  • Follow the rules of the road. Routes will be open to traffic. Please, NO headphones. The long route will ride on bike paths, so please ride single file and be courteous to other users. All routes are on heavily used bicycle and walking trails. Fair Hill Park is open to equestrians. Please talk to equestrians and ask how best to pass them. We want to be invited back, please be good stewards!
  • Sorry, NO REFUNDS. This is a rain or shine event and would only be cancelled if rider safety is at risk. If trails will be damaged, we will re-route the ride to gravel and hang out at Old Stone Cider!

Velo Amis is a non-profit organization. Since 2011, Velo Amis has donated over $404,000 to local non-profits, organizations and individuals involved in cycling and other outdoor activities. Proceeds from the Cider will be used to support the mission of Velo Amis Help us support #MoreKidsOnBikes #MoreGirlsOnBikes. to $45/$185 on 9/15/26 at midnight)

Our grand finale for the Rust Belt Ruckus CX Race Series comes back to One O Four Farm. This course is so good we race it twice!  Jon and Shannon always change things up so the course feels new and fresh even if you've raced it (every single time) like I have… It's rolling, has perfectly apexed turns through orchards and farm fields like flying through a labyrinth, and some punchy techy parts back by the beaver sanctuary. It really doesn't get much more fun than this for a cyclocross course.

Non Sanctioned, no USAC license required

All competitive racers need an approved helmet

Participants under 18 years of age are required to have a signed parental consent form.

NO PARKING ON ROAD (Rt. 104)

Please see confirmation email for exact event location and parking instructions.

Racing will start at 10:30am with a course designed specifically for our Junior racers and continue through our final race of the day ending at or around 2pm. 

We will allow day of registration but ask you to please pre-register if possible. These events take many volunteers to run successfully and any and all preparation that can be done ahead of time makes these days run much smoother. Double up and race a second race for only $15! 

Back for 2026: The Buffalo cyclocross promotors have teamed up with The Campus Cycling Collective (the organizer of this race) to bring you The Rust Belt Ruckus! : A Buffalo Cyclocross Series This will be race 3 of 5 in the series. If you'd like to register for the full series to save a few bucks and get all your registrations done in one shot, please go HERE! (Registration for series closes 10/9/26)

EventName: Rust Belt Ruckus 2026 - A Buffalo Cyclocross Series
EventNotes:
The Campus Cycling Collective, Inc. is proud to present The Rust Belt Ruckus! — A Buffalo Cyclocross Series

***Early bird pricing now until 9/15/2026 at midnight***

Adult Race Entry $40 -> $45 (after 9/15)

Adult 5 Race Series Entry $160  -> $180 (after 9/15)

Register early and save some hand up money!

**There will be day of reg at every event (cash only and $10 extra)**

*Individual Race Registrations are linked below*

Overview

Back for 2026 your Buffalo cyclocross promoters have joined forces with the Campus Cycling Collective to bring you a better cyclocross season. The Rust Belt Ruckus will consist of a 5 race series in a condensed season format going from October 11th to November 15th. (no more August 80 degree cross race followed by weeks of no local races) All races will be UNSANCTIONED, meaning you do not need a USAC license to participate, or worry about one day licenses. This removes barriers of entry for Canadians, former license holders who miss riding in the tape, and new racers. 

We will have consistent race schedules and a condensed “Siuta” format so the entire day fits into 3 ½ hours of racing. This will put more people on the course at once making it more fun, not a solo time trial. This also gets you back to your family or allows plenty of hang out time or to help set/clean up the course. 

Each race will have its own podiums and awards, but at the final race on November 15th at One O Four Farm's Gobble OOF CX, we will present series awards for those who participated and performed the most & best & worst,  along with some other CX Promoter picked superlatives…. You must complete 4 races to be included in series awards/results.

Event Schedule

The Rust Belt Ruckus consists of 5 independent cross races. The races take place in October and November across the WNY region. You may sign up for the entire 5 race series on this page (and save $40!). Or you can sign up for individual races using the links below.

  • 10/11/26 - Knox Farm CX (East Aurora) Race One
  • 10/25/26 - OOFF CX (Lockport) Race Two
  • 11/1/26 - Beaver CX (Grand Island) Race Three
  • 11/8/26 - JR West Falls CX (West Falls) Race Four
  • 11/15/26 - Gobble OOF CX (Lockport) Race Five & Series Finale

Adults race all 5 races for $160 (plus fees). For juniors it's only $60 (plus fees) 

These are the early bird fees. After 9/15/26 Adults registration increases to $185. 

You can add a second race at EVERY race for an extra $60 ($15x4 one free).

 

Race Day Schedule

  • 9:30 am Registration Opens
  • 10:30 am Race One: Juniors u15 (on a shortened course)
  • 11:30 am Race Two: Cat 4/5, SS, Women Open, Women 4/5
  • 1:00 pm Race Three: Open 1/2/3/4/5, Cat ¾ Men 1:15 pm: Masters 40+, 50+, 60+, 70+
  • Race Podiums will be done after each race.
  • At Race 5 / Series Finale, all podiums will be done at the end. This includes race and series level podiums.

Series Rules

The series consists of 5 races, but only 4 results are required for overall series rankings. We don't want a single mechanical to ruin your overall ranking. 

4 results required to be eligible for series rankings and awards. 

If you complete all 5 races, the worst result will be discarded.

 

If you sign up for the whole series you only need to register ONCE (on this page).  You will receive a discount that equates to ONE FREE RACE. And you will SUPPORT all of us Buffalo cyclocross promoters who stick our necks out & volunteer our time. All with an end goal of getting to rode around a field like we are all 12 years old, with you, having the time of our lives…

 

So, what are you waiting for? Sign up today and help us Bring The M*utha F*cking R*ckus!

Sponsors: @MTB.NY & Campus WheelWorks

[Give them a follow on Insta! ]

And keep an eye out for their banner on the race courses!

Please don't make us have to change your category to make you race your peers, because we'll do it in an embarrassing way.

 

The Deal

The venue is the really cool one that Crosstobeerfest is at except most of the course is on the other side, where it's too dark for a night race.  There are trails, ups, downs, berms, run-ups, run-downs, logs, man-eating squirrels, etc.

We also have music, craft beer, and a food truck so there will be no reason to leave after your race.  Unless you race in the last race, you'll then have to go home after you race.

Secret Squirrel Venue Map.

Please note there DOGS are NOT allowed on the grounds. Please do not bring your dog. We will ask you to leave,

The Donut Madison Relay 

The last "race" is the Donut Madison Relay.  We'll shorten the course down to only include the wooded section that's near the Start/Finish.  Teams of two will relay race.  The "waiting" racer will consume an entire donut when his/her partner returns before starting their lap, and so on.  This event is the final party of the day and is 20 minutes of hilarity.

One person registers both team members.  The other team member needs to complete their registration via an email that gets sent.  Don't forget!

 

 

Race Day Registration is an additional $20

WE'RE NOT JERKS!  IF YOU NEED A REFUND PRIOR TO THE EVENT AND HAVE A LEGIT EXCUSE YOU'LL GET IT.  JUST EMAIL US YOUR STORY

If you have to ask what category you should register in you are probably a NOVICE.  If you always win by a significant margin or have at any time worn special stripes then you are an ELITE.  If you know your USAC category then consult that, unofficially.

The Houston Round of the State CX series
Presented by 

Shoot for the stars at Space Cowboy Cross at the Pasadena Convention Center and Municipal Fairgrounds in Pasadena, TX – Part of the  TXCX series.

 If you are going to CX Nationals in Fayetteville, AR, Dec 10–14, 2025, earn USA Cycling points at this race and improve your starting position there.

Course Notes– packed with off-camber turns, and fast, flowy sections, mount “run up optional”.

Spectator Friendly - Plenty of parking, and most of the course is viewable from the finish area.

Want to try cyclocross? There is a category for everyone, including first-time racers.

 

Race rules:

  1. Don’t be a jerk.
  2. All USAC cyclocross rules apply.
  3. The promoter’s ruling is final.
  4. Gravel and mountain bikes without bar ends are allowed. No maximum tire widths enforced. 
  5. Please inform the officials if you withdraw from the race. 
  6. Awards will be awarded 3 deep in competitive categories. Depending on field size, the promoter may expand to 5 deep.
  7. Please support our sponsors.
  8. Check-in is required at registration each day to be counted in the results

 

Entry Fees

Entry fee is $45 for your first race and includes any additional races on the same day (ex. Novice riders may also enter the 3/4/Novice field on the same day at no additional cost).  Note: You must register for these at the same time to take advantage of this discount.

On-site registration will be available this year. Entries after midnight on Thursday, 11/19, will incur a $10 late fee and may not be included in call-ups. Registration closes 30 minutes before each race wave, so we highly encourage you to sign up as soon as you can. Call-ups will be by crossresults.com.

 

Racing Licenses

All competitive categories require a USA Cycling license to participate. If you do not have a current USAC annual license you can purchase one at memberships.usacycling.org.

 

 

Parking and Directions

Ample parking is available near the race course. Parking is between the RV park and the Rodeo arena. Please respect park speed limits and be aware of bicycles and pedestrians inside the park. 

 

Weather

The event is rain or shine. Delays or cancellations may be issued at the discretion of the promoter or race officials in the event of severe weather.

EventNotes:
MT. NEBO ENDURO | NOVEMBER 21-22, 2026

We’re excited to return to the stunning Mount Nebo State Park! The Mt. Nebo Enduro is a mix of technical and flowy singletrack with stages for all levels. Perched high above the Arkansas River Valley, Mount Nebo offers amazing views.

Registration opens Friday, June 12th at 8am with participation based on a first-come, first-served basis. To create a rewarding enduro race experience, organizers reserve the right to limit overall event participation. Each participant’s entry includes:

  • One-day competition with up to 4-7 stages and 10-20 total miles of rider-designed racing with dedicated pre-race practice times the day prior to the race.
  • Sufficiently marked courses with maps emailed to participants the week of the event.
  • Lively mid-race aid stations with access to professional neutral mechanics and medical support.
  • Professional event timing with accuracy to the 1000th of a second and instant results.
  • Complimentary post-race meal and cold beverages (21+ for adult beverages, ID required) in a family-friendly festival setting.
  • Awards ceremony by category with prizes awarded 5 deep.

RACE VENUE

Mount Nebo is a prominent, flat-topped mountain mesa located in west-central Arkansas near Dardanelle. Rising 1,762 feet above sea level and soaring 1,350 feet directly out of the surrounding Arkansas River Valley, it is entirely enclosed by Mount Nebo State Park. Established in 1927, it serves as Arkansas's second-oldest state park and is a premier hub for outdoor recreation. 

Venue Address: 16728 West State Hwy. 155, Dardanelle, AR 72834

 

EVENT SCHEDULE

Final event schedule with packet pickup, official pre-ride, and start times will be released the week of the event. Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When permittable, an official pre-ride/practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances.

Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine except under extreme circumstances. When possible, an official practice will be scheduled the day prior to Race Day(s). The Race Director reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances. 

 

DRY CAMPING - To book your campsite, visit the Arkansas State Parks reservation page. 

SAFETY - This is not the time to skimp on protective equipment. Helmets are required to be worn on course during official event times and we highly suggest a full-face helmet, knee pads, and elbow pads.

TEMPERATURE - In November, Mount Nebo, Arkansas experiences cool, crisp weather. Temperatures typically reach an average high in the mid-50s (50°F to 54°F) and drop to average nightly lows in the low-to-mid 30s (30°F to 35°F).

WATER & SNACKS - While hydration will be available at select locations on course, riders are encouraged to plan to carry at least 50-60 ounces of water and enough snacks to sustain themselves under strenuous exercise.

NICE TO HAVES - Bug spray, sunscreen, spare tubes, pump or CO2, plugs, patches and other parts.

DOGS - Dogs are allowed but are required to be on a leash at all times. No exceptions.

TRASH - If you pack it in, pack it out. We are guests. Please follow all event sustainability and recycling requests.

RACE DAY MEAL - A post-race meal will be provided to racers and volunteers on Race Days only. Redeemable meal tickets will be provided at the Registration & Timing tent. When possible, additional food trucks and other resources will be made available on-site for fans, family and friends.

WAIVER - All participants will be required to sign a waiver of liability prior to competing in the Arkansas Enduro Series.

REFUND POLICY - Arkansas Enduro Series events are rain or shine, and refunds will not be issued except under extreme circumstances. The Event Organizer reserves the right to adjust the schedule due to any unforeseen circumstances including rescheduling the event to a future date.

Every year an event comes along that tests mental and physical strengths of its racers like no other. Pisgah Productions proudly presents the hardest (and most fun) thing you will do this year….. the DOUBLE DARE.

Teams of two riders will race to reach up to 10 checkpoints (CPs) per day, two days in a row. The race begins at 10AM on Saturday and every team must be back before 10PM. The race resumes at 6AM Sunday with 10 brand new checkpoints. Every team must finish before 6PM on Sunday. Teams ‘in the running’ should expect up to 70 miles of riding with 12,000-15,000 feet of climbing each day.

SINGLE-DARE! The one-day category at Double-Dare!!! Teams of two riders will race up to 10 checkpoints, in any order, and return to the start/finish the fastest. Checkpoint locations will remain secret until start time and there is no suggested route. Start time for the one-day category will be 10AM Saturday and Final cutoff will be 10PM.

For both DOUBLE-DARE and SINGLE-DARE:

There will be nothing at the checkpoints other than pre-existing landmarks. Every team must carry a reliable digital camera to photograph the landmarks as proof of being there.
This is for all 10 races including the state championship.

Race Notes:

Start the year off with the 20th El Paso Puzzler.  Come on down to El Paso and enjoy our year around MTB weather.

Venue and course: for 2027 we are working with the land managers on the final venue arrangements and courses.

   50 mile race - 8:00am Saturday January 16th, 2027

   35 mile race - 8:30am Saturday January 16th, 2027

   15 mile race - 9:00am Sunday January 17th, 2027

   Kids race - 10:00am Sunday January 17th, 2027

All proceeds from the Puzzler are used to support the Borderland Mountain Bike Association - Not for profit, run by all volunteers.  We support our mountain and trail system with any money made!!

50 mile race, for top 5 overall finishers, both women and men paid equally

   1st place - $500

   2nd place - $300

   3rd place - $200

   4th place - $150

   5th place - $100

Categories:  We reserve the right to change the final categories based on registration numbers, but we typically have age categories for each race as: Juniors (under 18), 18-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60+ (race day age).

Prizes:  Our prizes will be EPIC this year again.

   50 Mile Race:  Along with the Cash Payouts listed above, Awards for 1st, 2nd and 3rd place for all categories.  First 75 finishers will receive a prize.

   35 Mile Race: Awards for 1st, 2nd and 3rd place for all categories.

   15 Mile Race: Awards for 1st, 2nd and 3rd place for all categories.

   Giveaways and raffle's throughout the event. <-- so anyone might be able to get other giveaways/prizes

Safety Cut Off Times: For the 35 and 50 mile course, we have cut off times that each racers must pass before this time or they will have to ride in the safety vehicle back to the venue.  This is to ensure that each rider completes the course in the allotted time and safely.  These times may change slightly based on final course routing.

  • Lower Sunset Parking Lot Aide Station (mile 13) - 1:00pm
  • Northwest Access Road (mile 23) - 2:30pm (north end of Lower Foothills)
  • If riding 50 mile race - Roundhouse (mile 35) - 2:30pm

Category Consolidation: Race director may combine race categories if there are not enough registrations to support each category.  We do not combine Male / Female categories.

Course Pre-riding: 99% of the El Paso Puzzler Course is within the Franklin Mountain State Park.  Your race day entry to the park is included in your registration.  If you are riding the course any other day, you must obtain a day use permit $5 per day per user.  Those permits can be obtained at the Iron Rangers (self pay stations) at any one of these trailheads (Lost Cow, Roundhouse or Chuck Heinrich Park), the park visitor center at the Tom Mays unit,  or online at  https://texasstateparks.reserveamerica.com/camping/franklin-mountains-state-park/r/deDetails.do?contractCode=TX&parkId=1200020  

Merchandise: All merchandise purchased online will be available for pickup at packet pickup times or the BMBA tent during the event.  There will be no shipping offered and any merchandise or packets not picked up after 30 days from the race will be considered a donation to the BMBA and will be used appropriately. 

Parking: Parking is limited at the venue and will be first come first serve.  Carpooling is highly recommended. $5 donation.

Spectators: All spectators entering the Franklin Mountain State Park will be required to pay the daily usage fee.  That can be paid via the Iron Rangers (self pay stations at the trailheads) or online at Here.  If paying online, please print the permit and have it on the dashboard of your vehicle.

Camping: Primitive camping will be open at the venue starting Friday at 1pm and closing Monday at 10am.

E-Bikes: This is an endurance race, so no form of E-Bikes are allowed.  Any rider who shows up with an e-bike will be disqualified and not permitted to race even in a noncompetitive manner.  There will be no refunds for disqualified riders.

Weather: Although the weather in El Paso is usually amazing in January, there is always the chance of race delays or cancellations due to weather.  We will do our best to hold the race on the dates scheduled.  If there is a weather event that does not allow for a safe race on Saturday or Sunday, the race will be moved to Monday.  If the race is cancelled due to weather there will be no refunds as this is a not for profit fundraiser.

No refunds for individual cancellations: If there is a risk that you may not be able to attend, we highly suggest you look into BikeReg Refund Protection, which can be purchased during checkout.  Make sure you review the details before purchase to see what cancellations are covered.  BikeReg does offer individual participant cancellation insurance if purchased during registration see here for details  https://www.bikereg.com/knowledge-base/104/Participant-Registration-Insurance--Allianz-Registration-Protection

Orange Blossom Gravel is all about the adventure... We consider this a non-competitive celebration of the lifestyle of enjoying bikes and community. And we welcome everyone. 

If you want to sign up for the 35 mile course and stop to smell the flowers, get some ice cream, and do some birding that's perfect. If you want to try and finish the 100 mile route in under 5 hours and push yourself that's totally fine too. We want to offer you the most fun experience possible, and fun is a relative term. 

As always, you'll be hitting up chonky pavement, glorious gravel, and surfing clay roads through beautiful, blooming orange groves. Let's explore the wonders of nature together while pushing our limits on two wheels and untamed terrain. All routes offer at least one support stop, with the 100 mile course offering two stops. 

100, 60, and 35-mile route options, plus a 5-mile kids and families route! 

Note: Y'all means ALL, and all y'all are welcome, as long as you come in the spirit of community, kindness, and respect. We encourage participants of ALL identities and will NOT tolerate discrimination against anyone —including our immigrant and transgender friends and family— in our online spaces, media, or at our event.
